exposure: Risk stratification at first prenatal visit
cohort: 41,044 singleton pregnancies at the Rotunda Hospital, Dublin, Ireland, from 2009-2013
finding: Neonatal encephalopathy was more prevalent in pregnancies assigned low-risk status at registration, suggesting that maternal and pre-pregnancy factors alone may not accurately predict fetal risk.
mod_finding: Low-risk women were more likely to have a spontaneous or operative vaginal delivery, while high-risk women were more likely to undergo cesarean delivery.
